summary:
Earthrise Atlas is an interactive educational website developed by a team of six students to explore places on Earth that resemble the Moon and Mars. The project aims to introduce planetary analog sites, where scientists can test equipment, conduct research, and prepare for future space missions. Using reliable scientific sources such as NASA, ESA, and USGS, the team collected information about 50 locations in Türkiye, 100 locations around the world, and 20 important planetary analog sites. The website highlights fascinating similarities between Earth and other planets, including Lake Salda in Türkiye and Jezero Crater on Mars.

The website offers interactive maps, side-by-side landscape comparisons, an AI-powered Mission Control assistant, gravity calculators, and educational quizzes to make space exploration engaging and accessible. The team used artificial intelligence to support the coding process while carefully checking scientific information for accuracy. Built using GitHub and Cloudflare, the website is freely accessible and automatically updates with NASA news. Through this project, the students aim to raise awareness of the importance of Earth's planetary analog sites and inspire young learners to discover how our planet can help humanity prepare for future missions to the Moon and Mars.
details:
Can we see Mars without going to Mars? We brought Earth’s “little Marses” and

“little Moons” together on one website.

Before going to space: rehearsals on Earth NASA calls places that resemble Mars and the Moon “planetary analogs”; it tests robots, spacesuits and astronauts in these places first. We brought these locations together on one website.
